sections.name: summary
sections.label: In short
sections.content: Confidence already grades care instead of gating work; the next step is confidence that grows from relationships and their strength, which nothing computes yet.

sections.name: body
sections.label: The evidence
sections.content: Decision 9d50126b (ratified 2026-10-24): "Confidence grades care, it does not gate work"; affirmation raises confidence instead of unlocking it. It came from a builder refusing srs-rust#1132 eighteen times for one missing line, and settled the contradiction logged as SP-104. The care policy (srs-programme docs/confidence-and-care.md, clerk lib/practice/care-policy.mjs) grades four axes high, medium or low, but every signal is a yes/no presence check, and the top Placement grade still needs an affirmed problem. The owner, 2026-10-27: "affirmation will just kill lots of this work. We build up confidence with cross checks, there is no fixed truth that will be affirmed" (c8b12a7b); 2026-10-23: domain assignment confidence (8ac535e5); 2026-10-30: "build up confidence based on the number of relationships and their strength". Gap: relation confidence was removed from the data model (srs decision 4f1e12e5, 0 of 250 relations used it) and RFC-046 did not restore it, so relation strength has no home. This joins the graph thread (part 4, relation integrity).

sections.name: open
sections.label: Open
sections.content: Where does confidence from cross-checks live: in clerk's care policy as a computed score, or in the data, which would reopen the 4f1e12e5 removal? What counts as a relationship's strength: its type, its source (owner words, measurement, agent), its age, agreement between independent sources?
